battle.name: 凡爾賽
battle.brief: 一九一九年六月二十八日下午，凡爾賽宮鏡廳內簽訂《凡爾賽條約》，第一次世界大戰的戰場被一份條約關上。美國遠征軍靠春田 M1903 栓動步槍加入西線，把同盟國逼入崩潰；條約卻把軍備上限、賠款、邊界同產能一併寫下，成為下一場戰爭的帳單。

kit.name: 春田 M1903
kit.history: 美國一戰栓動步槍。遠征軍大量使用，班火力仍靠機槍。

countries: 這場「戰爭」在1919年並非以陣亡收場，而是以條約收場，交戰方正是第一次世界大戰的兩大陣營。協約國一方以英、法、美三國為柱石，加上義大利、日本、比利時、巴西、塞爾西亞，以及英國自治領同英屬印度的代表，共有三十二個國家的代表出席一九一九年一月二十五日開幕的巴黎和會；德國被排除於談判之外，只能等文本送到手上簽字。真正拍板的是「四巨頭」：美國總統威爾遜、法國總理克列孟梭、英國首相勞合·喬治、義大利總理奧蘭多，其餘各國則在專門委員會裡處理航道、殖民屬地、邊界同少數民族問題。戰場上的一方是美軍遠征軍：一九一七年參戰之後，潘興拒絕把遠征軍拆散併入英法步兵營，改以師為單位保留獨立建制，第一、第二、第二十六與第四十二師先在凡爾登附近的大營區受訓，再投入西線。戰後歐洲湧現波蘭、捷克斯洛伐克、南斯拉夫、芬蘭、愛沙尼亞、拉脫維亞等新國家，它們既是「民族自決」的產物，也立即成為凡爾賽體系要防範的變數。
countriesEn: This 'war' did not end in 1919 with casualties but with a treaty, and the belligerents were the two great blocs of the First World War. On the Entente side the pillars were Britain, France and the United States, joined by Italy, Japan, Belgium, Brazil and Serbia together with the British dominions and British India, so that delegates of thirty-two countries attended the Paris Peace Conference which opened on 25 January 1919; Germany was kept out of the negotiations altogether and was allowed only to sign a text handed to it. The real decisions were taken by the Big Four: President Wilson of the United States, Georges Clemenceau of France, David Lloyd George of Britain and Vittorio Orlando of Italy, while the remaining states handled navigation rights, colonial possessions, frontiers and minority questions in specialist committees. On the battlefield side stood the American Expeditionary Forces: after entering the war in 1917, Pershing refused to break the AEF up into British and French infantry battalions and kept the division as the unit of independent organisation, with the 1st, 2nd, 26th and 42nd Divisions training first in the large camps near Verdun and then being committed on the Western Front. After the war a host of new states appeared in Europe, among them Poland, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia, Finland, Estonia and Latvia, which were at once the product of national self-determination and the very variable that the Versailles settlement was meant to contain.
people: 凡爾賽的四個關鍵人物背景各異。威爾遜帶著「十四點」赴歐，夢想用公開外交同民族自決取代祕密條約，最終卻被自己國內的孤立主義否決；克列孟梭是「老虎」，代表法國要求安全保證、萊茵非軍事化同巨額賠款；勞合·喬治代表英國，最關心海軍比例與海外商路，卻被公開反對戰爭的輿論牽制；奧蘭多代表義大利，主張「未受創的勝利」，對克列孟梭開出的代價極為不滿。南非的斯穆茨把國際聯盟的構想帶進會議。技術層面的幕僚同樣要緊：法方由外交部祕書長貝特洛把關文本，英方由外交部常務次官漢基統籌，美方則有威爾遜的顧問杜勒斯同國際法學者蕭特威爾參與起草與審閱。軍方代表是法國最高軍事委員會主席福煦，他關於德軍裝備上限的建議被寫進條約的軍備章節。德國一方的代表團由外交部長布羅克多夫-朗措領銜，他主張在保留異議的聲明下簽字，最終仍被迫在條約上落筆；代表團中的中央黨議員埃茨貝格爾成為德方的實際簽字人，並因此在一九二一年被右翼分子暗殺，付出了最高代價。
peopleEn: The four men who decided Versailles came from very different positions. Wilson went to Europe with his Fourteen Points, hoping to replace secret treaties with open diplomacy and national self-determination, and was in the end defeated by isolationism at home; Clemenceau, the Tiger, spoke for France and demanded security guarantees, the demilitarisation of the Rhineland and heavy reparations; Lloyd George spoke for Britain and cared most about the naval ratio and the sea lanes of world trade, while being constrained by a public opinion sick of war; Orlando spoke for Italy and pressed a 'victory without mutilation' against the price Clemenceau was asking. Jan Smuts of South Africa brought the idea of the League of Nations into the conference. The technical staff mattered just as much: the French text was steered by the Foreign Ministry secretary-general Berthelot, the British side was run by the Permanent Under-Secretary Hankey, and the American delegation had Wilson's adviser Dulles and the international lawyer Shotwell engaged in drafting and review. On the military side Foch, chairman of the Allied Supreme War Council, saw his advice on German armament limits written into the military clauses of the treaty. The German delegation was headed by the foreign minister Count Brockdorff-Rantzau, who wanted to sign while reserving the right to protest and was ultimately forced to put his pen to paper; Matthias Erzberger of the Centre Party became the effective signatory for Germany and was assassinated by the right in 1921 for it, paying the highest price of the delegation.
kits: 卡面這件春田 M1903 是美國陸軍在一戰的制式步槍，一九〇三年定型，口徑七點六二公釐的三十零六步槍彈，栓動原理，彈匣固定在機匣內部，一次五發，全槍連刺刀重約四公斤，槍身長約一點一三公尺，機械瞄具的表尺可刻到一千二百公尺，瞄準射擊每分鐘約十發，是當時產量最大、規格最統一的步兵武器。它同M1917自動步槍一齊供應遠征軍，M1918半自動型一九一八年才趕製了一小批，多數遠征軍師作戰時仍然使用栓動型。火力支柱其實不在步槍本身：步兵班火力靠勃朗寧M1917與M1919口徑三零機槍，砲兵大量使用法國七五野戰砲與美製七五榴彈砲，英軍則以十八磅砲配十八吋迫擊砲。遠征軍航空隊使用法製SPAD十三型與Nieuport二十八戰鬥機，坦克部隊整建使用法國雷諾FT輕坦克，海外的黑人部隊如哈林地獄旅團因配發限制改用法國貝蒂埃M1907/15步槍。戰後美國政府把大批春田步槍以低價處理，一九二〇至三〇年代大量流入拉丁美洲與民間市場，同樣的產能並沒有因停火而消失，這正是凡爾賽條約沒有處理到的部分。
kitsEn: The Springfield M1903 on the card was the standard rifle of the US Army in the war, fixed in 1903, firing the .30-06 cartridge of 7.62 mm calibre, bolt-action, with a five-round magazine housed inside the receiver, a weight of about four kilograms with the bayonet, a length of roughly 1.13 metres, a rear sight graduated to 1,200 metres and a rate of about ten aimed rounds per minute; it was the most heavily produced and most standardised infantry weapon of its day. It was issued to the AEF alongside the M1917 automatic rifle, while the semi-automatic M1918 was produced only in a small batch late in 1918 and most AEF divisions still fought with the bolt-action pattern. The real firepower backbone lay elsewhere: section firepower rested on the Browning M1917 and M1919 .30 calibre machine guns, artillery relied heavily on the French 75mm field gun and the American 75mm howitzer, and the British were matched with the 18-pounder and the 18-inch mortar. The AEF air service flew French-built SPAD XIII and Nieuport 28 fighters, the tank corps was equipped as a whole with French Renault FT light tanks, and Black troops overseas such as the Harlem Hellfighters were issued the French Berthier M1907/15 rifle because of supply arrangements. After the war the US government disposed of large numbers of Springfields at low prices, and in the 1920s and 1930s they flooded the markets of Latin America and the civilian trade; the same production capacity had not vanished with the ceasefire, and that was precisely what the Treaty of Versailles did not address.
tactics: 條約層面的戰術同戰場上的一樣講究節奏。巴黎和會自一九一九年一月二十五日開到六月二十八日，程序是全體大會、四巨頭小範圍磋商，再交各專門委員會與技術顧問逐條收窄；德國在五月提出異議，聯盟駁回大部分，並以恢復封鎖與追究軍備的後果相迫，最終文本在簽署前數日定稿，六月二十八日下午五時在鏡廳完成儀式，物理空間只有一張桌子與幾把椅子，過程卻被安排成供攝影全程記錄的宣傳場面。軍備解除是條約裡最硬的部分：盟軍派駐解除武裝委員會逐點清點德軍繳出與存留的槍砲，德軍必須按上限裁軍，海軍被限制在六艘主力艦、六艘輕巡洋艦與十二艘驅逐艦的規模，條約同時禁止德國製造或囤積化學武器、裝甲車、坦克與軍用飛機。戰場上被這份條約收束的那套美軍打法，是一九一八年下半年遠征軍在西線的做法：以連續的小單位攻擊消耗德軍縱深，第四十二師在七月的攻勢中以步兵連為單位向前穿插，砲兵集中火力壓制反斜面陣地，補給靠鐵路與卡車把砲彈、糧秣運到前線。停火之後，這些兵被解散，這些槍被清點，這些產線被限制，方法與節奏卻在別的國家繼續。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the treaty were as much about timing as the tactics of the battlefield. The Paris Peace Conference ran from 25 January 1919 to 28 June 1919, and its procedure was plenary session, small council of the Big Four, and then line-by-line narrowing in specialist committees and technical advisers. Germany lodged its objections in May, the Allies rejected most of them and held over the consequences of resuming the blockade and of pressing the armament clauses, and the final text was settled only days before the signature; at five o'clock in the afternoon of 28 June the ceremony was completed in the Hall of Mirrors, the physical space being little more than a table and a few chairs, though the whole business was staged so that cameras could record it as a public show. Disarmament was the hardest part of the treaty: an Allied disarmament commission counted the guns and artillery surrendered or retained by the German army piece by piece, the German army was capped, the navy was limited to six battleships, six light cruisers and twelve destroyers, and the treaty forbade the manufacture or stockpiling of chemical weapons, armoured cars, tanks and military aircraft. The American way of fighting that this treaty gathered up and closed was the AEF's method on the Western Front in the second half of 1918: small-unit attacks that wore down the German depth, the 42nd Division pushing forward with individual infantry companies during the July offensive, artillery massing fire on reverse-slope positions, and supply carried by rail and truck to bring shells and rations to the front. After the ceasefire those men were demobilised, those rifles counted and those production lines restricted, while the method and the rhythm carried on in other countries.
data: 可核對的數字集中在幾處。條約於一九一九年六月二十八日簽訂，正文四百四十餘條，簽署地點是凡爾賽宮鏡廳，距離一九一四年六月二十八日的薩拉熱窩暗殺正好五年。軍備方面，德軍總兵力上限十萬人，海軍限六艘主力艦、六艘輕巡洋艦、十二艘驅逐艦，並禁止生產化學武器、裝甲車、坦克與軍用飛機。賠款方面，賠款委員會於一九二一年五月五日訂立付款表，總額一千三百二十億金馬克；在此之前德國須先交付等值二百億金馬克的黃金、商品、船舶與證券，約合五十億美元。遠征軍傷亡方面，美軍遠征軍總傷亡約三十二萬人，其中陣亡五萬三千四百零二人、非戰鬥死亡六萬三千一百一十四人（多與一九一八年流感疫情相關）、受傷約二十萬四千人。封鎖在停戰之後又維持了八個月。產能方面，一九二一年德國武器出口佔中國進口武器的一半以上，金額一千三百萬馬克，德國公司另以「X預算」藏起最多相當於公開軍費一成的支出，一九二五年德國公司已開始設計坦克與現代火砲，一九二七年一月盟軍解除武裝委員會撤離之後，克魯普立即擴大裝甲板與火砲生產，到一九三七年德國軍品出口已達八千二百七十八萬馬克。
dataEn: The verifiable figures cluster in a few places. The treaty was signed on 28 June 1919, its text runs to some four hundred and forty articles, and it was signed in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, exactly five years after the assassination at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914. On armaments, the German army was capped at 100,000 men, the navy at six battleships, six light cruisers and twelve destroyers, and the manufacture of chemical weapons, armoured cars, tanks and military aircraft was forbidden. On reparations, the reparations commission drew up the schedule of payments on 5 May 1921 with a total of 132 billion gold marks; before that Germany had to hand over the equivalent of 20 billion gold marks in gold, commodities, ships and securities, about five billion dollars. On American casualties, the AEF sustained roughly 320,000 casualties, of which 53,402 were battle deaths, 63,114 noncombat deaths, largely from the influenza pandemic of 1918, and about 204,000 were wounded. The blockade was kept in place for eight months after the armistice. On capacity, in 1921 more than half of China's arms imports came from Germany, worth 13 million marks, and German companies hid spending in so-called X-budgets worth up to an extra tenth of the disclosed military budget; by 1925 German companies were already designing tanks and modern artillery, and after the Allied disarmament committee withdrew in January 1927 Krupp immediately expanded production of armour plate and guns, German military exports reaching 82,788,604 marks by 1937.
cause: 凡爾賽條約要解決的，是第一次世界大戰留下來的帳單與地圖。遠因是二十世紀初歐洲的同盟體系、海軍競賽與巴爾干火藥桶；引爆點是一九一四年六月二十八日的薩拉熱窩暗殺。直接導致開戰的是七月危機與各國總動員時刻表，戰爭的走向則在兩個轉折點上定形：一九一七年德國的無限制潛艇戰把美國拖進戰局，美軍遠征軍自一九一七年四月參戰，一九一八年上半年的德軍春季攻勢失敗，加上英法美在西線的反攻，使同盟國在物資與士氣上先崩；而俄羅斯帝國在布列斯特-立陶斯克條約中退出戰事，戰爭的目標與格局已被改寫，戰勝國再沒有共同的敵人可團結。停戰之後，列強各有算盤：法國要萊茵安全與賠款，英國要海軍比例與殖民地，美國的威爾遜要公開外交與民族自決，義大利要「未受創的勝利」，日本要山東權益，於是條約把戰爭責任、軍備限制、賠款、殖民托管與新國家的版圖一併寫定，連同一條要求德國接受責任的條文，變成日後爭論的源頭。
causeEn: The Treaty of Versailles set out to settle the bill and the map left by the First World War. The distant causes were the alliance system of early twentieth-century Europe, the naval race and the powder keg of the Balkans; the spark was the assassination at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914. The immediate cause was the July Crisis and the mobilisation timetables of the general staffs, and the shape of the war was fixed at two turning points: Germany's unrestricted submarine warfare in 1917 drew the United States in, the American Expeditionary Forces entered the war in April 1917, and the failure of the German spring offensive in the first half of 1918, followed by the Allied counter-offensive on the Western Front, broke the Central Powers in supply and morale; meanwhile the Russian Empire left the war in the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, and once the aims and the alignment of the war had been rewritten the victors had no common enemy left to unite against. After the armistice each power played its own hand: France wanted security in the Rhineland and reparations, Britain the naval ratio and the colonies, Wilson of the United States open diplomacy and national self-determination, Italy a victory without mutilation, Japan its rights in Shantung. The treaty therefore wrote down war responsibility, armament limits, reparations, colonial mandates and the map of new states in one stroke, and the clause that made Germany accept responsibility became the seed of every later quarrel.
impact: 凡爾賽體系的影響，一半是制度的，一半是怨恨的。制度上，國際聯盟在一九二〇年成立，托管制度把德國殖民地改為英法比等國代管或瓜分，奧地利、匈牙利、南斯拉夫、捷克斯洛伐克等新國家的邊界在條約中被確認；德國則被剝去殖民地、萊茵非軍事化、軍隊限十萬人，並被要求接受最高軍備委員會的裁軍審查。怨恨上，美國參議院在一九一九年十一月以五十三票對三十五票否決批准條約，條約對美國不生效，美國改以一九二一年的獨立對德和約處理雙邊關係；義大利未得阜姆與達爾馬提亞；中國因山東問題拒絕簽字，國內隨即出現五四運動；德國則在國內把戰敗歸咎於背後捅刀，替凡爾賽制度背負了本不屬於它的罪名。軍備與產能上，條約限制的是國家行為而非工業能力，德國公司把軍火生產轉到荷蘭、瑞士、瑞典，「X預算」把支出藏進帳外，一九二七年盟軍解除武裝委員會撤離後，德國的裝甲板與火砲生產立即恢復，一九三〇年代重整軍備已是公開事實。一戰的武器帳單並未因簽字而清零，條約只把它推遲了十幾年。
impactEn: The effects of the Versailles settlement are half institutional and half a matter of resentment. Institutionally, the League of Nations was founded in 1920, the mandate system turned the German colonies into administered or divided possessions of Britain, France and Belgium, and the frontiers of Austria, Hungary, Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia were confirmed in the treaty; Germany lost its colonies, was demilitarised in the Rhineland, was limited to 100,000 men, and was made subject to disarmament inspection by the Supreme War Council. In the register of resentment, the United States Senate rejected the treaty in November 1919 by 53 votes to 35, so it never entered into force for the United States, which instead concluded a separate peace treaty with Germany in 1921; Italy received neither Fiume nor Dalmatia; China refused to sign over the Shantung question and the May Fourth movement followed at home; and Germany blamed the war on a stab in the back, which saddled the Versailles system with a charge that was not really its own. On armaments and capacity, the treaty constrained state conduct rather than industrial capability: German firms moved arms production to the Netherlands, Switzerland and Sweden, X-budgets kept spending off the books, and once the Allied disarmament committee withdrew in 1927 the German production of armour plate and artillery resumed at once, with rearmament an open fact in the 1930s. The weapons bill of the war was not settled by the signature; the treaty only deferred it by a dozen years or so.
result: 一九一九年六月二十八日下午，德國代表在凡爾賽宮鏡廳的條約上簽名，戰爭狀態至此以文本終止，條約在德國代表團保留異議的情況下生效，而要求聽取德國意見的相關條款始終未獲執行。簽字之後的結果並不整齊：義大利未得阜姆，德國未得殖民地，戰勝國之間因法國的海軍主張與義大利的東亞要求再起爭執，這份條約被當時人形容為「沒有一方滿意的妥協」。軍備條款在紙面上切得乾淨，德國工廠拆毀、軍械封存、海軍縮編，但限制只約束政府行為，工業產能與技術人員四散到外國，條約生效後不到十年，德國重新組軍，萊茵蘭在一九三六年已有部隊進駐，軍備條款在實質上早已名存實亡。從兵器角度看，春田 M1903 完成了它的任務：這支量產的栓動步槍在美國遠征軍手上構成了一支能在西線獨立作戰的步兵，協約國的戰勝因此不再單靠英法的人力與砲兵；而真正決定這場「戰爭」最後走向的，是條約第一百八十一條起的一組解除武裝作業，用清點、拆卸、搬運同文件，而不是用戰鬥。
resultEn: On the afternoon of 28 June 1919 the German representatives signed the treaty in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, and the state of war ended there in the form of a text, entered into with the German delegation's reservations and accompanied by clauses for hearing Germany that were never executed. The results after the signature were untidy: Italy did not get Fiume, Germany got no colonies, and the victors quarrelled again over French naval claims and Italian claims in the east; contemporaries described the treaty as a compromise that satisfied nobody. The armaments clauses were clean on paper, with German factories dismantled, weapons sealed up and the navy cut back, but the limits bound only the conduct of governments, while industrial capacity and skilled technicians scattered abroad; within less than a decade of the treaty coming into force Germany was rearming, and troops were in the Rhineland by 1936, so that the armament clauses had long been real only on paper. Judged from the point of view of the weapon, the Springfield M1903 had done its job: this mass-produced bolt-action rifle, in the hands of the American Expeditionary Forces, made up an infantry that could fight independently on the Western Front, and the Entente's victory no longer rested on British and French manpower and artillery alone. What really decided the final course of this 'war' was the disarmament work set out in the clauses from Article 181 onward, carried out by counting, dismantling, hauling and paperwork rather than by battle.
